steps.name: PyDESeq2 Wald test with log fold change shrinkage
caveats: The input is already a gene-level Salmon count matrix; no transcript-level quant.sf files are present, so the tximport length-offset import of R-0018@a472 cannot be applied. State this limitation in the report: a gene-level matrix cannot detect differential transcript usage, and isoform-length effects are uncorrected.

The user constraint is Python-only, so the R apeglm/edgeR implementations are unavailable. Use pydeseq2's lfc_shrink (its MAP/adaptive shrinkage implementation, the Python analogue of the apeglm path) and name the estimator actually used in the table header; keep the unshrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE beside it (R-0009@f54e, R-0085@c24d).

PyDESeq2 does not ship DESeq2's independent filtering; implement it in the script (filter on the mean normalized count, choosing the threshold that maximizes discoveries at alpha 0.05, DESeq2-style) or state explicitly in the report that only BH without independent filtering was applied. With 6 replicates per group, DESeq2/Cook's logic sets p-values to NA for flagged count outliers rather than replacing counts; report the count of such genes (R-0039@e17a).

Do not apply an effect-size threshold post hoc; if an LFC threshold is wanted it belongs inside the test (R-0037@e6d8). The research question does not state one, so the primary selection is padj < 0.05.

plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney: DE + TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human kidney bulk RNA-seq samples (6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle control) as raw gene-level Salmon counts (12,000 genes x 13 CSV columns, first column gene symbol) with a 12-row metadata table. The question — which transcription factors drive the treated-vs-control response — decomposes into (1) a sample-structure QC on a blind variance-stabilizing transform to verify grouping and outliers before any test, (2) a two-group differential expression fit (PyDESeq2 Wald, median-of-ratios size factors, explicit reference level, Cook's outlier flagging, BH at alpha 0.05 with an independent filter) that produces the Wald statistic of every tested gene, and (3) transcription-factor activity inference with decoupleR's univariate linear model on that full contrast statistic against the CollecTRI human regulons (DoRothEA A-C as a secondary regulon set for robustness). Small design (12 samples, single batch, no covariates) means regulons must come from prior knowledge only, not from network inference on the study itself. All scripts are Python (pydeseq2, decoupler); the language constraint rules out the R edgeR-QL second-method overlap, so robustness is carried by the CollecTRI vs DoRothEA regulon comparison instead. The report step assembles the DE table (unshrunken and shrunken LFC, SE), fit diagnostics, the p-value histogram, and the ranked TF table with a reproducibility record.
